title: Why Do Ferns Have Brown Dots? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya turns over a leaf of the corridor fern and finds rows of brown dots underneath. Is the plant sick? Not at all: those dots are full of spores. This lesson covers pteridophytes, the ferns and their relatives, from NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 3, Plant Kingdom.

You will see why pteridophytes were the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem, animated as water and food moving), a live zoom ladder from the fern to a leaflet, a sorus and one sporangium where meiosis makes spores, and the five stages from spore to prothallus to a new fern, with antherozoids swimming through water. We compare homosporous and heterosporous plants (Selaginella, Salvinia) and why that is a first step towards the seed, then microphylls, macrophylls and strobili, and the four classes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida and Pteropsida. Then a worked example, the exam trap about the main plant body, an original NEET assertion and reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 24 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
